title: Manchester United increase ticket prices for fourth successive season with five per cent rise
content:
Manchester United will increase season ticket prices for the fourth successive year next season in the club’s latest attempt to drive revenues.

In an email sent to season ticket holders on Friday, United said Old Trafford prices will be increased by five per cent across all areas for the 2026-27 campaign at an average of £2 per game for adults and £1 per game for under-16s.

Around 600 general admission tickets in the Sir Bobby Charlton Stand will also be relocated to another part of Old Trafford to accommodate additional hospitality seating.

United say that the relocation of the supporters is also related to work that is required to be carried out on the dugouts to meet UEFA regulations for the club’s next European campaign.

The season ticket price rises include corporate and hospitality tickets, although United’s executive club members are able to freeze at the current price if renewing their membership before April 15.

United said the increases should be viewed in the context of the club having a “clear objective to return Manchester United to the top of domestic and European football”.

“We want to keep investing in the team and improving our facilities so fans get the best possible experience,” a club statement read. “We also need to make sure the club stays financially sustainable taking into account inflation and rising costs.”

United have not increased the minimum seat usage policy for season tickets, meaning fans will still need to attend, forward, list for resale or donate the cost of their seat for at least 16 of 19 Premier League matches.

The club will also reintroduce ticket collection for European away games next season, subject to European qualification, following feedback from supporters.

In a statement, the Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST) expressed its regret at another year of price increases, following rises in the 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 seasons.

“It is disappointing that the club has ignored our call, as part of the FSA’s league-wide campaign, for a ticket price freeze. Supporters are paying more and more to watch their team, and as the FSA campaign said: enough is enough,” a MUST statement read.

“We’ve also learned that 600 more loyal fans are being moved for ever more hospitality. Those people will be understandably furious, and need to be better treated by the club than those who went through the same thing last year were.

“That said, we are pleased the club listened to some of our concerns and there are no further restrictions on season ticket holders forwarding their tickets and no increase in the minimum usage rules. Football clubs make better decisions when they listen to fans — they should do it more!”
